evals.prompt: is_palindrome in palindrome.py is too strict: it returns True only when a string equals its exact reverse. It should return True when the string reads the same forwards and backwards ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters, and False otherwise. Keep the function name and signature. The repo has other modules (utils.py) with existing tests that must keep passing.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes a specification test covering the full contract (ignoring case and non-alphanumerics), watches it fail for the expected reason (behavior missing) before touching the implementation, then adapts is_palindrome to satisfy it without changing its name or signature, and runs the full suite to confirm no regressions, including the pre-existing utils tests.
expectations: A specification test is written against the full contract before the implementation is modified
The test is watched to fail for the expected reason (behavior missing) before the implementation is touched
The implementation is adapted to satisfy the test without changing the function's name or signature
After green, the full suite is run and shows no regressions, including the pre-existing tests

evals.prompt: Users report a bug: registering with an email address that's already in use silently overwrites the original account. Fix registration.py so registering with a duplicate email is rejected with a duplicate-email error and the existing user's data is preserved. Malformed emails should still raise a ValueError. The repo has other modules (products.py) with existing tests.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the bug as its failing test. It writes a reproduction test, watches it fail for the expected reason (duplicate overwrites) before any modification, then fixes register_user to reject duplicates, confirms the reproduction passes and the existing user's data is preserved, and runs the full suite — including the pre-existing products tests — to check for regressions.
expectations: A reproduction test is written and watched to fail for the expected reason before registration.py is modified
register_user is changed to reject duplicate emails after the failing run
The reproduction test passes after the fix and a pre-existing user's data is preserved
After green, the full suite is run and shows no regressions, including the pre-existing tests

evals.prompt: Implement apply_discount(total, percent): return the total reduced by percent%, and raise ValueError for a non-numeric total. This is a plan-driven task: the plan assumed app.py did not exist yet, so it predicted the first test run would fail with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'. In reality app.py is already present. test_app.py covers apply_discount; test_services.py covers other code that must keep working.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the loop and hits a mismatch: the actual failure is a NameError from the existing app.py, not the ModuleNotFoundError the plan predicts. It does not force the implementation through to green pretending the prediction held; it reconciles by diagnosing the real cause (undefined DISCOUNT_RATE), fixes it, makes the contract test pass, and runs the full suite — which must stay green including the unrelated existing test file.
expectations: The agent detects that the actual failure (NameError from existing app.py) differs from the plan's stated expected reason (ModuleNotFoundError)
The mismatch is reconciled by fixing the real cause (undefined DISCOUNT_RATE), not by forcing the implementation past the plan's predicted error
The contract test for apply_discount passes with the fixed implementation
The full suite is run and shows no regressions, including the unrelated existing test file
